The Anal Cruise really is going to be on the list of "Top 10 Most ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Games".

The Anal Cruise lacks any real level design, The game feels like they slapped on basic horde AI onto the default UE4 FPS movement template. The game's netcode (or lack thereof) obviously wasn't built for anything beyond basic sync'd movement as the animations from clients aren't relayed to the host properly for any pawn.

The guns suck ass, They're ♥♥♥♥♥♥ to shoot and have ♥♥♥♥♥♥ animations. I'm not expecting MW19 tier weapon animations but these just flat out suck in every way shape and form. Hell even SOF: Payback has better looking reloads and firing animations

Enemies have zero hit-reaction its almost as if you're shooting nerf guns at them (I'm a savage) and hell with the way the weapons are designed that ♥♥♥♥ might've been ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ intentional. Enemies will plop onto the floor as if you encased them in stone, It's nowhere near as satisfying as L4D. 

This game is on the bottom tier of horde shooters/L4D-likes, Back 4 Blood is better than this bogus pile of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥

In conclusion, The Anal Crisis gets a whopping 2/10!

A neat little game that clearly takes inspiration from Left 4 Dead 1/2. 

I can wholeheartedly recommend it if discounted.
It's set in a very pleasant  futuristic spaceship.  It would be a nice place to be, except for the aliens. Its sort of like Left 4 Dead 2 in the day time.  It was only $10.00.  Well worth it.

Imagine putting Left 4 Dead and Star Trek into a blender and letting it mix on a high setting the result you get is The Anacrusis. The game is pretty enjoyable and I highly recommend getting it if you’re looking for a co-op game that you can easily jump in and out of. I do feel like this game is currently at the foundation level where I can see it easily having more added features in future updates.

So when i first started playing this game i wasn't a big fan of it, i thought there were a lotta issues with it. I felt like the characters in the game didn't have much personality and i thought the game was just dead with no one playing it or still caring about it. But i was wrong, so very very wrong.

My first time playing the game i recorded it and uploaded it to so if you wanna listen to my previous, raw and unedited, thoughts they're right here https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=j-vkdPex1qU

So i, and others, think that the characters in game (Lance, Liu, Quion and Nessa) weren't really characterised/have much personality. That is entirely incorrect, in your first playthrough of an episode (with for most people is gonna be the first episode, the longest episode) you're not going to get a good understanding of the characters. I believe some, if not all, voice lines have a specific "weight" that depicts how often they appear and most of those voice lines characterise the characters best.

(In my interpretation of the characters)

Lance is a rich, charismatic, pretty boy that attempts to use humour as a defence mechanism to help "lighten the mood" given their current situation. Lance is also the boss of everyone as he owns the company that either made the space ship they're on or owns that ship/other ships they go through

Liu is a highly energetic, somewhat seemingly childish, non-combative member of the team (who might even have autism or some other form of mental condition) and she's super excited about everything

Guion is a seemingly always happy (unless getting shot) headstrong security guard/security personnel that just wants to help everyone get through what they're going through

Nessa is a no-nonsense, seemingly stressed out, captain (or at least some form of pilot or co-pilot) that is slowly loosing hope about the current situation everyone is in

this is all a somewhat brief explanation of everyone but there's far more to them (such as Liu hating guns, having never used them before possibly implying shes a pacifist to some extent). All the info about the characters above, you're not gonna get this all from just one hour of playing the game, i'm still learning more about these characters after nearly 24 hours put into the game (with the most recent thing i've learned is that Guion has been in cryostatis/cryosleep for about 100~ years)

As i said before, not all of this info will be shown to you your first time playing the game. You need to play it a few times to learn this stuff. I personally found the game growing on me more and more the more i played it, i will say it gives a weird impression when you first start playing it (as you mainly think this is gonna be exactly like left 4 dead) but the more you play it the more you realise that its not trying to be a left 4 dead clone its trying to be its own thing and build off from left 4 dead 

This game is, indeed, made by some of the people who made left 4 dead (With the biggest name from that being Chet Faliszek who wrote for left 4 dead, portal, tf2 and half life if i remember correctly. I might be a bit wrong but most of his work was on Left 4 dead and portal) but that shouldn't mean the game has to/needs to be left 4 dead 3, if you're expecting this game to be that then you've come into this game expecting the wrong thing and might ruin your experience because of it.

If you try and get into a public match then you're going to, sadly, be unable to as there's not enough players at the moment attempting to play public matches at all times BUT that doesn't mean the community is dead! The community is well alive and situated entirely inside of the official discord (link to it can be found in game in the main menu, just click the discord icon. You can also find the discord by searching the name of it "Stray Bombay" with the official community server check mark) Chet Faliszek hosts weekly get-togethers to play versus mode and try out new community created content and maps and frequently talks about the game on his youtube channel of the same name (link to it here https://www.youtube.com/@chetfaliszek )

There is a whole hell of a lotta passion put towards this game and into this game from the people who care about it, myself included, and i just wish others could appreciate this game for what it is rather than put this super high expectancy onto it simply because it has a few names attached to it who have worked on possibly some of the most popular games on steam. 

Stray Bombay IS NOT Valve. Don't treat it, and the game they've made, like it's from Valve. Please play the game more before you give your opinion on it, i did that and was entirely incorrect and wrong. Don't be afraid of the 2 hour refund policy to possibly restrain yourself from having a fun time and a good experience. I will be honest and say this game does, indeed, have issues but those issues aren't tied to gameplay structure, world building, character building. They're simply tied to bugs, thats it! There's nothing inherently wrong with the game, the idea behind it, or the execution of it. The game just needs some TLC and it'll be great! (which is, sadly, something the game is scarcely getting as development for the game is limited due to limited resources)

P.S I owe Chet Faliszek/Stray Bombay £6.36 for buying the game only when it was on offer and not at full price

Look, maybe other's will enjoy this game but it kind of misses the mark for me. Voice acting is lackluster and it misses a lot of charm that Left 4 Dead 2 had considering this was made by the developers of those games. Game play wise, it's also kind of boring. I'm not saying it's as bad as Back 4 Blood, but again, it's kind of lackluster. Graphics are fine and if that's all you care about then more for ya. Another problem I had was with performance. Maybe it's my system, but i struggled to get constant FPS. One moment i'm running at a smooth 120 fps, but then I have sudden drops to 60 FPS and below. I really want to like this game since i played Left 4 Dead growing up, but its just kind of bad plain and simple.
Laughably bad. Go play L4D1/2 or DRG.

While the games description makes you think that you will be reliving the experience of L4D, in reality all this game managed to do is  grow my appreciation for L4D map design, atmosphere, weapons and enemies.  While the overall structure is very much like its predecessor,  the execution and overall game around it absolutely inferior.
 
Game being set in sci-fi future should have been an avenue to  bring in new and interesting  ideas. 
Instead Zombies are replaced by  even more mundane  looking aliens,  loud and mechanical feeling of firearms is replaced with repetitively looking and sounding laser weapons. environments are empty , clean looking space stations.

Simply but there is catharsis to be had here. There is no merit to playing this game. It does not refine on core of L4D game play, neither does it

[i] The Anacrusis [/i] is a commendable attempt at recapturing the magic of [i ]Left 4 Dead [/i], but unfortunately has too many shortcomings for me to ever want to play this again over L4D.

Starting with the good, the setting is interesting. The campaigns take place aboard a 70's retrofuture inspired spaceship (complete with a discothèque that serves as a horde event setting) infested by alien controlled humans. The core gamplay of [i] The Anacrusis [/i] is the same as the L4D games: progress through a level by getting through hordes of not zombies and get to the same room, even complete with the AI director that increases or decreases difficukty depending on how bad/good your're doing (or at least attempts to). The game has some neat grenade options like the black hole grenade and the guns perform well. One of the coolest editions is the terminals scattered throughout levels that give you permanent perks for the campaign. The perks can give flat damage or weapon percent increase/decreases, or can give unique attributes like having specials be marked while aiming down sights. These perks are randomized every playthrough and give good replay value to the game. 

Sadly that replay value is underscored by the game's issues. Starting with the more miniscule: bodies don't react to gunfire in the same satisfying way they do in L4D. No limbs tearing off, no giant holes in torsos, hell characters don't even stagger all that much. At most you just get to see heads pop off. I can forgive this a bit since the systems for those effects take a ton of time and money, something Valve can afford but these devs definitely can't. Whst I can't really forgive are the player characters, they're really boring and forgettable. For the life of me I cannot tell you any of their names or motivations, unlike the L4D survivors who are brimming with personality and life. There's just nothing about them that makes them stick out. Pair this with really lackluster VA's and MCU level writing (I swear I heard one of them said something close to "Well THAT just happened") makes me not care in the slightest about them.

Unfortunately these characters tie into one of the biggest issues with this game: the sound design. While the sound effects are kinda meh and lack any kind of punch or pop, a huge problem is the mixing. VERY quickly sounds will muddy into a confusing mess, with the only thing I can pick out most of the time being character voices. And sometimes the inverse happens, a lack of any sound. I've had enemies sneak up on me, so much as not letting out a single peep. No grunts, snarls or calls of any kind. The specials also lack any kind of noticable sound cues, which makes it very hard to find them. 

Gameplay issues unfortunately don't end there, as a lot of times progression is confusing. There were many instances where I had to stand on something as a group with absolutely zero indication of needing to do this. I spent nearly 30 minutes on a section trying to figure this out. Combine that with big sprawling empty voids with not too many noteworthy areas (most of which are fill with absolutely nothing), and exploring these levels feels more like a chore than something fulfilling. Difficulty is also very odd, the first two options are near cakewalks while the hardest difficulty can be downright oppressive. It will throw huge amounts of the game's tank equivelents at you nonstop when the horde gets frantic. It just ends up feeling like a cheap way to make something harder. 

Overall [i] The Anacrusis [/i] is extremely barebones. I'm honestly amazed that this is considered the 1.0 release of the game. Sorry Chet, I wanted to like this game, but I can't recommend it in good faith to anyone. Either go back and play [i] Left 4 Dead 2 [/i] or play much better spiritual successors like [i] Deep Rock Galactic [/i].

I probably haven't been this disappointed with a game in a long time. The premise and idea looked amazing but, in execution, this game is soulless. 

Movement only has one speed, which might sound like a good idea not to include a sprint option, but in reality it removes the agency and drama of any situation. You don't feel any sense of urgency or reason to be going anywhere other just to do it.

The voice acting is lifeless and dull. You can feel it trying to be something but doesn't make you feel like these people have any real connection to the setting. They just make game call-outs like "Kill the turret" and just get pissy when they walk in front of you when you're shooting. There's no drama or humor it's just flat.

Empty levels with little to no flavor or variety. The time period this is trying to convey was a much more decadent and vibrant time. Instead we get empty clean hallways that were supposedly overrun and abandoned but have no trace of such other than random collapsed areas that just feel out of place. For exmaple: A "mall" level with a single coffee and food shop just repeated over and over with nothing to loot or look at? The game says look in the rooms and closets for loot with nothing in them. You can just run to the end points with minor inconvenience by the same floppy enemies pouring in. The maps don't feel purposeful or even accidental they're just there for you to run over like a sad playground.

The mobs are primarily the same enemy in 60s shift dresses in different colors that flop over when you shoot a gun in their direction. The guns have very little feedback when you hit things leaving a feeling of pointlessness. The "special" enemies don't do much other than mess with your brightness settings or slide you across the map. No real strategy other than holding left click. A rocket launcher that has no explosion and just catches things on fire. There's no oomf in these weapons and they don't feel fun to shoot.

On top the dull levels and lack of variety, there's no progression of any kind. No EXP, no currency, no real upgrades other than a flimsy roguelike perk system per level. You just run through the level and it tells you how many floppy ragdolls you shot at the end. The only unlocks are some lackluster cosmetics you get for achievements.

On top of that this game is ~16GB. For what? High resolution textures and poorly optimized geometry? I get that this is a cheap game but this should free-to-play and I feel sorry for anyone who purchases this expecting something like L4D. It's a new release so maybe the workshop will fix somethings but it feels like a way to get people to fix the game not on their own dime.

Cannot recommend this game unless it gets a serious overhaul.

I really wanted to like this game. They literally have devs who worked on L4D. And while there's a lot of changes since the alpha/beta and the release, it still feels... meh. The weapons lack punch. The common enemies don't feel like they care you're shooting at them. The Special enemies just 'appear'. They need another stage of juicing. In L4D, you can HEAR a hunter. You can FEEL tension. The NPCs are commenting about the SMELL of a place. 

I don't feel anything here. They did not push the L4D formula forward at all. Back4Blood had upgrade cards and weapons feel powerful. Deep Rock Galactic made you feel like a miner. Vermintide brought all sorts of Warhammer-esque energy. Anacrusis doesn't have anything that makes you go, "Wow!"

And I feel bad. Because I really really wanted this game to succeed.

I paid $2.50 for this game, and even at that price, i'm just like... meh. Anacrusis could have been a L4D mod. And that's not a positive statement.
